maya: Onboarding polestar-8b-hybrid (llama-ish attention + mistral heads). fp16 baseline looks fine but quantized int8 build is producing very odd summarization behavior on the news & legal evals.

felix: What odd means quantitatively?

maya: RougeL drop ~0.06 absolute, QA F1 down 0.10, but ppl improved from 11.4 -> 10.0. generation stutters, repeats a clause, then injects an unrelated sentence chunk.

ara: Improved ppl with worse task metrics almost always points at position/rotary mismatch or tokenizer mis-alignment. Did conversion change head ordering or rotary mode?

maya: I used the standard converter:
```bash
python convert_polestar.py \n  --src checkpoints/polestar_fp16.pt \n  --out converted/polestar-int8/ \n  --quant int8 \n  --rotary global_scale \n  --normalize_toks NFKC
```

eval-bot: run summary: polestar-int8 v0 -> rougeL: 0.43 (fp16 0.49); qa_f1: 0.70 (fp16 0.80); ppl: 10.0 (fp16 11.4).

ara: two things to inspect quickly: 1) head map and rotary per-layer metadata in meta.json; 2) tokenizer normalization vs training (NFKC vs NFC). If tokenizer differs, token boundaries shift causing sentinel or EOS to appear mid-sentence.

maya: meta.json excerpt (from converted dir):
```
{"n_heads":"32", "head_map": "flattened", "rotary_mode":"global_scale", "rotary_scale":0.9, "vocab":"polestar-v2"}
```

ara: head_map == "flattened" smells like converter reshuffled to canonical order. Polestar was trained with grouped heads (group_size=4) and used a head-permute in preproc. Runtime still expects grouped order for kv-cache. That will corrupt the cross-attention coupling.

sasha: Also check embedding matrix alignment: some of these hybrids had tokenizer offsets (char->byte) nonzero. Verify tokenizer.offset_table and compare to original repo.

maya: tokenizer.json shows "normalization": "NFKC" while training repo lists "NFC". I'll rebuild tokenizer with NFC and re-run.

felix: While you do that, try a controlled convert with --preserve-head-order true and set --rotary-mode to "headwise" then run the small deterministic warmup prompt; compare logits to fp16 warmup run. Script:
```bash
for m in headwise global_scale; do\n  python convert_polestar.py --src checkpoints/polestar_fp16.pt --out /tmp/conv-$m --quant int8 --preserve-head-order true --rotary-mode $m\ndone
```

maya: queued two converts now. Also capturing one decode with --no-kvcache to see if repetition persists without cache.

dev-bot: deploy: converted/polestar-int8-v0 pulled to staging at 1759990022.

eval-bot: queued evals 1759990030 and 1759990040.

maya: results: headwise + preserve-head-order -> rougeL 0.48, qa_f1 0.78, ppl 11.1. global_scale kept -> rougeL 0.43, qa_f1 0.71, ppl 10.0. No-kvcache decode removed the token-misalignment repeats but produced slightly lower fluency.

f elix: So preserving head order + headwise rotaries recovers most task metrics but ppl rose toward baseline. That confirms converter reorder was the culprit.

ara: Action items: 1) make converter default to preserve_head_order when model metadata indicates grouped_heads or head_permute present; 2) emit head_map array in meta.json (explicit mapping); 3) include per-layer rotary_scale if present instead of single global value; 4) auto-detect tokenizer normalization mismatch and warn during onboarding; 5) add CI warmup logits equality test (small epsilon).

maya: I'll open PR with those changes and add a small onboarding smoke that fails if ppl decreases but rouge/qa drop beyond thresholds (heuristic flag).

sasha: Also add a bulk-scan job to find converted artifacts with head_map == "flattened" and schedule re-conversions where training metadata indicates grouped_heads.

dev-bot: PR created by maya: #4881. CI started.

eval-bot: rerun after NFC tokenizer + headwise convert -> polestar-int8-v1 -> rougeL 0.49, qa_f1 0.79, ppl 11.05. Sample decode aligns with fp16 reference: "The committee voted unanimously..."

maya: good. I'll sweep other recent onboards tomorrow. tagging @eng-oncall just in case staging shows regression.

end of thread
